comparator.name: Human Resource Studies: People Management
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: 60 compulsory ECTS in year 1, 60 compulsory ECTS in year 2, and year 3 with a genuine 30-ECTS mobility window plus 30 compulsory ECTS, including comparative labour relations, social philosophy, cross-cultural HRM and a 12-ECTS thesis. Zero-credit GROW development is excluded, and no content is invented for the open mobility space.

Mobility Window: exchange, internship or minor
Genuine 30-ECTS mobility, internship or minor space; no elective content is invented.

core: International people management, strategic HRM and evidence-based organisational policy
Organisational psychology and sociological analysis of people, work and organisations
Talent, employee development, workplace health and well-being
Human-resource analytics, qualitative and quantitative research, causal analysis and evidence-based consulting
International labour relations, cross-cultural HRM and the social and economic dimensions of work
adjacent: International organisations, European employment institutions and cross-cultural workforce governance
questions: How can international organisations balance employee well-being, development and performance?
How can analytics and research improve evidence-based people-management decisions?
How do cultural and European institutional contexts shape labour relations and workforce policy?

candidates.label: Workplace psychology, well-being and talent development
International labour relations and workforce governance

selection.assessment: The closest programme owns international and strategic people management, cross-cultural HRM, people analytics, evidence-based policy and the social-economic dimensions of work. Organisational psychology, well-being, talent and employee development form a coherent second route, while comparative labour relations and workforce governance form a distinct institutional route. Both exceed the 30-ECTS distinctness floor. Three alternatives is the maximum, and every generator-eligible interest has one construction owner.

alternatives.label: International people management & strategic HRM
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates organisations, leadership, psychology, sociology, economics, international business, communication and research around evidence-based people management.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Human Resource Studies: People Management: an interdisciplinary international programme on people, work and organisations combining strategic HRM, organisational psychology, sociology, economics, leadership and evidence-based research.
progression: Foundations in economics, politics, law, sociology, psychology, organisations and research precede advanced organisational psychology, leadership, negotiation, public economics, social theory, international business and applied inquiry. Existing validated schedules respect prerequisites and planned offerings; seven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Workplace psychology, well-being & talent
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum centres psychological science, employee health, development, talent and assessment while retaining organisational leadership, sociology and research.
alternatives.concept: A workplace-psychology and talent direction focused on employee health, well-being, development, assessment and social behaviour, supported by organisational leadership, sociology, communication and empirical methods.
progression: Behavioural, biological, social, organisational and research foundations precede statistics, cognition, lifespan development, health, abnormal psychology, psychodiagnostics and advanced organisational leadership. The component schedules are reused from validated UCR pathways and retain prerequisite order and planned availability; eleven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, fourteen courses shift the centre of gravity from strategy, business, economics, law and organisational communication to behavioural science, health, development, assessment and psychological research. The difference exceeds the 30-ECTS floor.

alternatives.label: International labour relations & workforce governance
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum gives sustained weight to employment institutions, European and international law, governance, political economy, sociology and cross-border organisational contexts.
alternatives.concept: An international workforce-governance direction examining labour relations and people policy through law, politics, European institutions, economics, sociology, organisational research and international business.
progression: Introductory politics, history, sociology, economics, law and research precede constitutional, European and international law, political economy, advanced institutions, social theory and independent inquiry. The schedule is reused from a validated UCR pathway and respects prerequisites and offerings; seven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, thirteen courses replace leadership, psychology and organisational communication with constitutional and international law, European history, political institutions, social movements and transnational governance; it also differs from the workplace-psychology route by eighteen courses.

notes.text: Tilburg prescribes a dedicated international People Management sequence with talent management, work-and-health psychology, analytics, evidence-based consulting, comparative European labour relations, cross-cultural HRM and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can construct coherent interdisciplinary routes in international people management, workplace psychology and labour institutions, but it does not reproduce the complete specialist HRM or methods sequence; the 30-ECTS mobility window remains open.
